paper.title: Harnessing Pre-Resolution Signals for Future Prediction Agents
paper.central_claim: Revisiting the same unresolved question yields pre-resolution signals (temporal contrasts across checkpoint notes) that, written as bounded typed patches into a persistent question-local F/E/U harness, improve later forecasts before resolution beyond repeated prediction alone; scope limited to within-question adaptation, with post-resolution check and cross-question transfer not quantified.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; model_type is the configured slot only

rationale: 题内预决议对比信号→有界F/E/U护具写回；NH/GH/同日对照支持题内增益，但n小无区间、跨题与决议后校验未测、主表算力不对等。

evidence.quote: As the same unresolved question is revisited, Milkyway extracts pre-resolution signals from evolving evidence and repeated forecasts, uses them to update the harness, and improves later forecasts on that question before resolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: label-free (pre-outcome) signals from revisits drive harness updates that improve later forecasts of the same question.

evidence.quote: Realized outcomes are valuable for judging final correctness, but they provide weak process-level credit assignment
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: delayed, coarse outcome-only supervision in prior forecasting learners.

evidence.quote: ACE evolves long-form context from execution feedback
evidence.support_explanation: Closest neighbours named by the authors (ACE, Reflexion, ExpeL, Meta-Harness, AutoHarness); all use post-hoc execution/outcome feedback, not within-question temporal contrasts.

evidence.quote: The harness stores only reusable procedural guidance.
evidence.support_explanation: Persisted object is procedural text (axes F/E/U), explicitly not answers/evidence.

evidence.locator: Sec 3.3 Harness update from the signal
evidence.quote: the runtime accepts at most one validated patch per checkpoint, rather than unconstrained iterative free-form rewriting
evidence.support_explanation: Bounded edit rule; with Table 4 (<=2 adds/patch, <=5 entries/axis, null op, fixed apply order).

evidence.quote: The applier validates entry references, filters updates that are clearly redundant with active entries
evidence.support_explanation: Only structural/duplicate validation gates retention before resolution; no measured-utility admission test.

evidence.quote: the paper does not separately ablate this stage or quantify later cross-question reuse of checked guidance
evidence.support_explanation: The outcome-based retain/revise/deprecate check (Eq. 9) is specified but unevaluated; the retention gate is therefore unmeasured.

evidence.quote: Milkyway is intentionally limited to typed, question-local harness updates within a single unresolved question.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated scope: no cross-question retention, no tool/workflow change.

evidence.quote: NH removes persistence and measures repeated forecasting alone.
evidence.support_explanation: NH control isolates repeated forecasting; GH (next) isolates typed vs free-form persistence; FH is the method.

evidence.quote: GH keeps persistence but replaces the typed harness with a free-form memory blob under matched byte and write-call budgets.
evidence.support_explanation: Generic-memory control; but GH is one hand-built control, not an ACE/Agent-KB-style editor.

evidence.quote: Repeated forecasting under matched compute therefore explains only part of the rise, and free-form persistence does not recover the effect of typed writeback.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2: FH-NH endpoint gains +13.1/+9.1/+9.3/+11.0 and FH-GH +8.0/+9.1 on four cells with n=35/28/28/28 (GPT-5.4 05-05, 05-06; Qwen3.5, GLM-5.1 05-06); GH missing for open backbones.

evidence.quote: Because the editor needs at least two earlier checkpoint notes, no condition can consume non-empty writeback before T-2d; the earlier checkpoints therefore serve as built-in pre-writeback controls.
evidence.support_explanation: Delayed-separation prediction is a real distinguishable prediction (pre-writeback controls).

evidence.quote: Any change across rounds is attributable to rerunning, stochasticity, or in-arm state evolution rather than calendar-evidence drift.
evidence.support_explanation: Same-day control, n=28: NH 54.4/40.1/32.5/52.9, GH 57.0/46.8/42.9/44.8, FH 51.0/41.5/43.6/56.7 -> round-to-round swings of 10-20 points, comparable to the claimed +9..+13 effects; FH gain 5.7 < half of calendar-ladder gain.

evidence.quote: reports the per-question average tool-call count, prompt-token count, and LLM-call count at T-1d for each (backbone, date) cell of the main mechanism table.
evidence.support_explanation: Compute-matching evidence is for the main agent at T-1d only (FH within about 5% of NH); the editor call and cumulative cost over checkpoints are not reported.

evidence.quote: the memory blob is non-empty under the same persistence budget, but contains no explicit typed-harness schema vocabulary.
evidence.support_explanation: Artifact audit that GH did not reconstruct the typed interface.

evidence.quote: matched-budget GH writes a memory blob that locks in the opposite interpretation
evidence.support_explanation: Single resolved case (Hebei inbound share, gold 4.48; FH 5.24 vs NH 27.18 / GH 27.30): shows mechanism for one question only; also shows persisted text can lock in a wrong reading.

evidence.quote: Milkyway is evaluated in its deployed question-level loop: each scored question is revisited three times under the forward-only protocol, and the last checkpoint is reported.
evidence.support_explanation: Milkyway uses three revisits per scored question; single-run baselines get one run.

evidence.quote: provide strong search-and-scaffold baselines with no question-local persistence across checkpoints
evidence.support_explanation: Single-run baselines have no multi-checkpoint access; unequal compute/information vs Milkyway's three revisits.

evidence.quote: For self-evolving baselines, we provide only warm-up from resolved data preceding the scored slice and freeze the resulting state during scoring.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-evolving baselines do not evolve on the evaluated slice, unlike Milkyway's within-question evolution; Table 1 is end-to-end, not a component ablation.

evidence.quote: Under this protocol, Milkyway with GPT-5.4 attains the best FutureX overall score and leads on L1–L3.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1: FutureX Ovr 60.85 vs MiroFlow 57.55, best self-evolving 53.80; FutureWorld overall 69.05 vs 66.27 / 60.84; Milkyway does not lead L4 (45.85 vs MiroFlow 46.80) or FutureWorld binary/smc.

evidence.quote: No method sees outcomes from the scored questions before scoring.
evidence.support_explanation: Live prospective protocol; harness built only from earlier-checkpoint notes of the same question.

evidence.quote: Only resolved FutureWorld questions with valid retrieved ground truth are scored; unresolved questions are excluded from the mean.
evidence.support_explanation: Official scorer definition (option-F1; clipped squared-error numeric); exclusions flagged (216 scored for main slice; 28/50 and 35/50 scored/launched in mechanism cells).

evidence.quote: The mechanism study uses selected daily cohorts with matched pre-resolution checkpoints.
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanism evidence rests on two selected resolution dates (05-05, 05-06); selection criterion not stated; version label 'milkyway_v5' suggests iteration whose tuning data is not declared.

signatures.object: question-local typed harness H=(F,E,U) of (axis,when,guidance) procedural entries; baseline: BaseAgent under fixed prior B with no persistent state
signatures.information: public info up to checkpoint tau_t; fixed-schema checkpoint notes n_1..n_t (prediction, rationale, evidence/verification route, unresolved concerns); current H. Realized outcome NOT visible; answers/raw evidence excluded from H
signatures.operation: editor LLM contrasts n_t with earlier notes -> signal I_t (prediction divergence + diagnostic findings) -> patch Delta_t (add/revise/deprecate/null) -> deterministic Apply
signatures.output: H_{t+1} presented as a structured guidance block at the next checkpoint
signatures.conditions: t>=2; <=1 patch/ckpt, <=2 adds, <=5 active entries/axis; duplicates and bad references degrade to no-ops; apply order deprecate->revise->add
signatures.feedback: temporal contrasts among the model's own repeated forecasts under evolving public evidence (no label)
signatures.selection_rule_data: structural validation and redundancy filter only; no measured-utility or held-out admission before resolution
signatures.persistence: question-local H only; notes/signals/patches transient; per-checkpoint versions logged (legacy_versions)
signatures.later_use: predictor at tau_{t+1} on the same question
signatures.claimed_effect: later-checkpoint FutureWorld score rises more under FH than NH/GH (Table 2); end-to-end best on FutureX/FutureWorld (Table 1)
signatures.failure_boundary: no cross-question reuse; a wrong early lesson can persist (GH case shows lock-in; FH lock-in not analysed); signal noise from LLM self-diff unmeasured

signatures.information: H_{T+1}, notes N_{1:T}, realized outcome y
signatures.conditions: specified only; no implementation details of the rule
signatures.failure_boundary: unevaluated; not_applicable to the experimental claims

gap.author_gap: Forecasting agents learn from realized outcomes that arrive only after resolution and give weak process-level credit (what to track, verify, keep uncertain).
gap.checked_gap: Supported as a real limitation of outcome-RL/Future-as-Label style learners per the paper's own related work; residual bottleneck is within-question adaptation before resolution. Closest-neighbour texts (ACE, Reflexion, Agent KB, MemEvolve) are not in the pinned package, so the check relies on the authors' characterisation.
gap.lineage: Reflexion/ExpeL/Voyager/GEPA (editable text state) -> ACE/Agent KB/MemEvolve (evolving context/memory from execution feedback) -> Meta-Harness/AutoHarness (harness as optimisation target); forecasting side: ForecastQA/FutureX/FutureWorld benchmarks -> Halawi, outcome-RL, Future-as-Label (post-resolution supervision)
gap.closest_adjacent: ACE and Agent KB/MemEvolve (post-feedback context/memory), Reflexion (verbal reflection across trials); they use outcome or execution feedback; none uses revisit contrast with delayed ground truth per the authors
gap.residue: whether the contrast-derived signal beats generic reflection across revisits; cross-question retention; reliability of early lessons
gap.stakes: forecast quality on open questions where labels arrive late
gap.method_response: typed bounded harness writeback from note-history contrasts
gap.remaining_gap: no contrast-vs-single-note ablation, no cross-question or post-resolution evaluation, small-sample evidence
unresolved: neighbour full texts absent; test-time reflection without labels (Reflexion/Self-Refine style) not compared

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In small matched FutureWorld cells, bounded typed harness writeback from note contrasts raised later same-question forecasts over no-persistence and free-form-memory controls at matched main-agent compute; end-to-end leading scores under an unequal-compute protocol.
assessment.author_claim_vs_supported: Author claim (gains stem from pre-resolution-signal-driven harness evolution rather than repeated prediction alone) is supported in direction within-question; contrast-signal specificity, cross-question retention, outcome check and statistical reliability are not.
assessment.note: retained is scoped to within-question later checkpoints (not independent held-out tasks); no improver-level evidence.

G.reason: Real, specific gap (outcome-only, delayed supervision gives no process credit) and the changed object (question-local procedural guidance state) is named; neighbours (Reflexion/ExpeL/ACE/Agent KB/MemEvolve/Meta-Harness) are covered by name. Not 4: no analysis of why generic multi-round self-reflection/refinement across revisits (which needs no outcome either) is insufficient; neighbour full texts not in the pinned package.

M.reason: Chain note-contrast -> diagnosis -> bounded typed patch -> deterministic apply -> next-checkpoint conditioning is reconstructable, and yields distinguishable predictions (delayed separation, typed vs blob, procedure-not-answer). Weakness: signal quality rests on an LLM's reading of its own note diffs; changes in predictions may reflect new evidence rather than a procedural lesson, and nothing screens harmful lessons before use.

X.reason: Operation chain, information boundary (notes transient, only H persists), edit vocabulary, caps, null op, fixed apply order and per-checkpoint versions are specified. Gaps: no measured admission/rollback before resolution, outcome check unimplemented/unevaluated, no conflict-resolution beyond duplicate filter; Appendix D prompt/schema boxes are empty in the pinned HTML.

E.measurement.reason: Official FutureX scorer and a fully specified FutureWorld scorer on live prospective questions; outcome unknown at prediction time. Exclusions disclosed (resolved-only; numeric items without 8-point history dropped; 28/50 scored). Timing/budget of baseline runs on FutureWorld not specified.

E.causality.reason: Matched NH/GH/FH cells with fixed backbone/scaffold/tools/context/schedule, built-in pre-writeback controls, same-day repeated-round control, compute footprint and GH artifact audit address 'repeated prediction alone', calendar drift, extra compute and generic persistence. Not 4: no ablation of the contrast signal vs per-checkpoint reflection, no alternative editor/ACE-style writer under the same schedule; Table 1 comparisons confound 3 revisits vs single runs.

E.holdout.reason: Live forward-only protocol with outcomes unseen, harness built only from earlier same-question notes; baselines warmed on preceding resolved data. Scope limited: no cross-question or independent-task retention test, mechanism cohorts are two selected dates, tuning history of 'milkyway_v5' undeclared.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes and scored/launched counts are reported, and the same-day control reveals negative/flat arms, but no intervals, seeds or tests; the same-day table shows NH swinging 54.4->32.5->52.9 at n=28, comparable to the claimed FH-NH differences. Four small cells from two dates.

E.cost.reason: Per-question tool/token/LLM-call footprint at T-1d matched within about 5% of NH, supporting 'no extra compute' for the main agent. Editor-call cost, cumulative cost across checkpoints, and Milkyway's 3x revisits vs single-run baselines in Table 1 are not accounted.
